entries.proposition: Trial design: two-arm randomised observer-blind phase IIb trial of pre-emptive treatment in children diagnosed under four months, with neuropsychological outcome as primary.
entries.snippet: The clinical trial is designed as a two-armed, randomized, observer-blind, controlled phase IIb clinical trial for children < 4 months of age at inclusion.

entries.proposition: The control group receives standard care only, with no placebo, on the advice of the national regulator to reduce burden on neonates.
entries.snippet: no placebo will be administered to the control group. This directive was aimed at reducing the study-associated burden by avoiding daily intake of sham medication and reducing the number of required laboratory examinations.

entries.proposition: Blinding is of the outcome assessor only: an external observer who knows nothing of treatment, and caregivers asked not to disclose their group.
entries.snippet: Neuropsychologic testing and scoring will be performed by a blinded external observer, not involved in other study procedures.

entries.proposition: Randomisation is 1:1 by block, stratified by age group at inclusion.
entries.snippet: randomization is stratified by age groups (0 to < 2 months vs. 2 to < 4 months).

entries.proposition: Exposure is pharmacokinetically guided to a trough-level target range, with a prespecified adjustment table.
entries.snippet: Sirolimus trough levels will be measured at each study visit and dose adjustments will be made to achieve serum target levels of 5–10 ng/ml.

entries.proposition: Primary endpoint: Bayley-III cognitive scale at 24 months, two-sided Mann-Whitney test, 60 randomised; a 15-point difference is judged relevant.
entries.snippet: an improvement of 15 points in the BSID-III cognitive scale at the age of 24 months (e.g. a score of 75 in the control group and a score of 90 in the treatment group) will be considered relevant for reducing neuropsychological impairment

entries.proposition: Secondary endpoints are descriptive: adaptive behaviour, autism scale, checklists and seizures analysed by group and time point.
entries.snippet: the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales 3 (VABS-3) and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule 2 (ADOS-2) total scales as well as selected respective subscales will be analysed descriptively by group and time point

entries.proposition: The Background states controlled clinical trials of pre-emptive mTOR inhibition in infants under 2 years are lacking.
entries.snippet: Pre-emptive initiation of mTOR inhibitor treatment may mitigate TSC-related neuropsychologic deficits, but controlled clinical trials in infants under 2 years are lacking

entries.proposition: Timeline: recruitment began in Q1 2024 and the overall duration is expected to be 82 months; an initial safety analysis follows five treated patients.
entries.snippet: The overall duration of the clinical trial is expected to be 82 months. Recruitment of subjects started in Q1 2024.

entries.proposition: The authors state the trial could turn symptomatic management into a disease-modifying approach.
entries.snippet: this trial could fundamentally transform the therapeutic management of TSC-related neuropsychiatric manifestations from a symptomatic to a targeted disease-modifying approach.

entries.proposition: Protocol: no interim analysis for efficacy or futility; a data safety board meets repeatedly.
entries.snippet: No interim analyses regarding efficacy or futility are planned

entries.proposition: Protocol sample size: 60 randomised from 120 assessed assuming 50 percent willingness.
entries.snippet: To randomize 60 patients, 120 patients need to be assessed for eligibility assuming 50% willingness to participate in the trial.

entries.proposition: Protocol power: more than 95 percent only under a standard deviation of 15; falls to about 62 percent at a standard deviation of 25.
entries.snippet: Assuming that 30 patients per group can be randomized, a difference of 15 in the cognitive scale of BSID-III

entries.proposition: Fig 1: schematic of screening, eligibility, 1:1 randomisation to standard care or standard care plus the drug, visits and assessments.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1 flow chart: inclusion and exclusion criteria; Eligible? yes or no; Screening; Randomisation 1:1; control arm standard of care and intervention arm standard of care plus the study drug; study visits 1 to 12 plus end-of-trial visit; clinical assessments, neuropsychological evaluation at 12 and 24 months with BSID-III, ADOS, VABS, TAND and M-CHAT-R, laboratory examinations, safety assessments with PK sampling, and EEG and abdominal sonography.
